classification.difficultyReason: Use axis intercepts or a point on the circumference to determine the squared radius, including negative coordinates and a surd radius.

content.prompt: Determine the equation of each circle. They are all centred at the origin.

spec.description: Origin-centred circle with four labelled intercepts and positive-end axis arrows; no grid or ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied diagram remains visible; equation is answer-only.

spec.description: Origin-centred circle with four labelled intercepts. The source's missing minus sign at the left intercept is corrected.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied diagram remains visible; equation is answer-only.

spec.description: First-quadrant radius triangle with dashed vertical leg, right-angle mark and empty outlined leg-length boxes beside the vertical leg and below the horizontal leg.
spec.mathematics: P=(5,12); horizontal length 5, vertical length 12, radius 13. Point lies exactly on the circle.
spec.answerVisibility: Coordinates and radius label are supplied; both length boxes and the equation remain unanswered.

answer.worked:
The triangle has horizontal length $5$ and vertical length $12$.
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=5^2+12^2\\r^2&=25+144\\r^2&=169\end{aligned}$$
Hence $x^2+y^2=169$.

spec.description: Third-quadrant radius triangle with dashed vertical leg and right-angle mark; length boxes lie above the horizontal leg and left of the vertical leg.
spec.answerVisibility: Coordinates and radius label are supplied; length boxes and equation are unanswered.

answer.worked:
Side lengths are positive: the horizontal length is $3$ and the vertical length is $4$.
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=3^2+4^2\\r^2&=9+16\\r^2&=25\end{aligned}$$
Hence $x^2+y^2=25$.

spec.description: Second-quadrant radius triangle with dashed vertical leg and right-angle mark; length boxes lie left of the vertical leg and below the horizontal leg.
spec.answerVisibility: Coordinates and radius label are supplied; length boxes and equation are unanswered.

answer.worked:
The horizontal length is $7$ and the vertical length is $24$.
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=7^2+24^2\\r^2&=49+576\\r^2&=625\end{aligned}$$
Hence $x^2+y^2=625$.

spec.description: Fourth-quadrant radius triangle with dashed vertical leg and right-angle mark; length boxes lie above the horizontal leg and right of the vertical leg.
spec.answerVisibility: Coordinates and radius label are supplied; length boxes and equation are unanswered.

answer.worked:
The horizontal length is $20$ and the vertical length is $21$.
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=20^2+21^2\\r^2&=400+441\\r^2&=841\end{aligned}$$
Hence $x^2+y^2=841$.

spec.description: Circle with positive-end axis arrows and a labelled first-quadrant point; no supplied radius, projection, grid or ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Point is supplied; equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
Using the right-angled triangle from the origin to $(3,4)$:
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=3^2+4^2\\r^2&=9+16\\r^2&=25\end{aligned}$$
Hence $x^2+y^2=25$.

spec.description: Circle with positive-end axis arrows and a labelled fourth-quadrant point; no supplied radius, projection, grid or ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Point is supplied; equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The right-angled triangle has horizontal length $1$ and vertical length $3$.
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=1^2+3^2\\r^2&=1+9\\r^2&=10\end{aligned}$$
Hence $x^2+y^2=10$.
